mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals monetary easing, which lowers discount rates on equity cash flows, boosting expected returns and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the relationship reverses during high inflation periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate below 4.5% signals labor market strengthening, boosting consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not rise significantly when the trigger occurs (p > 0.05 in t-test) or the drop is not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in both demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) indices indicates a robust economic expansion, reducing uncertainty and driving upward pressure on equity prices, resulting in positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: both GDPC1 and INDPRO increase in the same month
failure_condition: The 60-day returns do not correlate positively with the co-movement of GDPC1 and INDPRO (Pearson r < 0.3) or the effect is reversed in contractionary periods.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, persistent low federal funds rates amplify growth expectations, leading to elevated S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS remains below 2% during a late-cycle expansion regime
failure_condition: The 5-day returns are not significantly higher than average during late-cycle expansions when FEDFUNDS are low (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% signals tightening monetary policy, raising long-term interest rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.0% and stays for 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not decline significantly when the trigger occurs (p > 0.05 in t-test) or the rate rise is not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payrolls increase exceeding 140,000 indicates strong labor demand, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits, which drives positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns do not rise significantly when the trigger occurs (p > 0.05 in t-test) or the increase is not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in both personal consumption (GDPC1) and housing demand (HOUST) signals broad-based demand expansion, reducing uncertainty and driving upward equity returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: both GDPC1 and HOUST increase in the same month
failure_condition: The 60-day returns do not correlate positively with the co-movement of GDPC1 and HOUST (Pearson r < 0.3) or the effect is reversed in contractionary periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in supply (INDPRO) while demand (GDPC1) rises indicates potential market imbalances, leading to short-term volatility but ultimately positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days as investors anticipate correction.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases while INDPRO decreases in the same month
failure_condition: The 20-day returns do not rise significantly when the trigger occurs (p > 0.05 in t-test) or the effect reverses in contractionary periods.
